title: When a Deal Dies at the 50-Yard Line

 When a Deal Dies at the 50-Yard Line
Hi Sara,
I’m in the middle of my busiest season ever, and this week, three deals died.
All three had cleared diligence. Purchase agreements were drafted. We were basically at the 50-yard line…and then, poof.
If you’ve ever made it that far and still watched a deal fall apart, you know how brutal it is. 
Here’s what kills deals that are THIS close to closing:
1. A surprise pops up

Think lawsuit, data breach, or a key employee walking out.
It might not even be a big deal, just bad timing. When something hits late, there’s no time to get clarity. Buyers bail. Solid reps and warranties can save you here by forcing disclosure upfront.
2. Overlawyering

A $300K asset purchase does not need a 90-page agreement.
If your legal team has no business sense, the deal can stall out fast. Sellers walk. Buyers burn out. And you’re left with redlines and regrets. 
A good lawyer should help you close, not just edit.
3. Last-minute deal breaker

Even with a solid LOI, big terms sometimes surface late, like indemnity or personal guarantees.
If the gap’s too big and no one will move, the deal’s done. Painful, but better now than post-close.
Want more real talk about how deals get done—or don’t?

I share weekly insights from the front lines. And if you missed this week’s video, it’s live now on YouTube.
To fewer landmines,
Sara Sharp
Deal Attorney & Founder of Deal Academy
